start.text: Keep your voice down. That goose on the billboard? My landlord reports to it.

company.text: The Powerful and Evil Goose Corporation. Their legal department insists that is the full name. Please keep your voice down. They own the walls.

choices.text: Why put Evil in the name?

reading.text: Ask Leo about The Quarterly Honk, or Ray about who owns the lodge. Some houses have books on ponds and executive waterfowl. Read carefully. Quietly.

leave.text: Of course. Walk casually. Do not make eye contact with the billboard.

start.text: Do you ever think we might be in a simulation? Somebody would have had to put all these little yellow flowers here. I like that idea.

choices.text: What if nobody put them here?
What would you put in a simulation?

end-1.text: Then I get to like the flowers anyway.

end-2.text: More warm afternoons. And one enormous dog.

start.text: If this is a simulation, do you think people are still out there when you stop seeing them? My friend moved away. I keep thinking how nice it would be if I could load a day when she was still here.

choices.text: What would you do that day?
Have you talked to her since?

end-1.text: Ask her to wait while I caught up. We always walked home too fast.

end-2.text: We wrote each other letters. I should write another one.

start.text: Sometimes the clouds look so deliberate that I wonder if we’re in a simulation. I’d be all right with that. Whoever chose the fog also remembered the smell of toast.

choices.text: What do you think they forgot?
Would you want to know for sure?

end-1.text: A way to stop the smoke alarm before the toast burns.

end-2.text: Maybe on a rainy afternoon, when I had time to think about it.
